** *
Jagmohan Bansal, Judge (Oral)

1. The petitioners through instant petition under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India are
seeking setting aside of impugned ex-parte assessment order dated 30.03.2005 (Annexure P-9) and
subsequent demand notices issued by the respondent.

2. Succinctly, facts of the case necessary for adjudication of the present petition are that daughter of petitioner No.1 solemnized marriage with Jagdeep Singh Sandhu, son of Baljit Singh Sandhu on 31.12.1996.

The couple could not enjoy their married life and relations got so sour that wife i.e.
daughter of petitioner No.1 lodged FIR No.3 dated 01.01.2001 under Sections 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086409-DB CWP-10469-2005 (O&M) -2- 406, 498-A, 313, 315 and 511 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') at Police Station Division No.4, Ludhiana against her husband and in-laws.

In the FIR, it was recorded that the petitioner has spent a sum of 8 Lacs apart from Mohinder Singh & Anr vs Income Tax Officer & Ors on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119969237/
1 giving other articles at the time of marriage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent-Income Tax Department on the basis of aforesaid FIR initiated proceedings against the petitioner alleging that he has concealed his income.
The proceedings were initiated in terms of Section 147 & 148 of Income Tax Act, 1961 (for short '1961 Act').
Petitioner No.1 at the time of initiation of proceedings and thereafter was in a vegetative state, thus, could not join the proceedings and subsequently passed away on 01.05.2005.
Respondent-department knowing the fact that petitioner No.1 cannot join the proceedings, passed impugned ex- parte assessment order.

The respondent by impugned assessment order made addition of 30 Lakhs in the returned income of the petitioner No.1.
3.
Mr. Pankaj Jain, Senior Advocate submits that matter arising out of aforesaid FIR stands amicably settled.

This Court vide order dated 27.01.2001 passed in CRM-M-35352 of 2010, Jagdeep Singh and others v. State of Punjab and another, on the basis of compromise arrived between the parties, has set aside aforesaid FIR.

entities.text: Jagdeep Singh and others v. State of Punjab and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The matter has been amicable settled between the parties and there is no finding by Criminal Court to the effect that petitioner had given/spent a sum of 30 Lakhs on the occasion of marriage of his daughter.
The respondent has created ex-parte demand and that too on the basis of FIR.

The respondent has not conducted an independent investigation 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086409-DB CWP-10469-2005 (O&M) -3- or brought on record evidence to the effect that petitioner had actually earned aforesaid income which was not disclosed in the Income Tax Return.

4. Per contra, Mr. Ranvijay Singh, Senior Standing Counsel for Income Tax Department submits that petitioner was duly served notice under Section 148 read with 147 of 1961 Act, however, he did not participate in the proceedings.
Left with no other option, the Assessing Officer passed impugned assessment order.
The petitioner had alternative remedy of filing appeal, however, he opted to file the present writ petition before this Court.
5. We have heard the arguments of learned counsel for both sides and perused the record with their able assistance.
6. The conceded position emerging from the record is that the impugned assessment order was passed on the basis of aforesaid FIR lodged by daughter of petitioner No.1.
The daughter of petitioner No.1 solemnized marriage with Jagdeep Singh Sandhu which miserably failed.
Daughter of petitioner No.1 lodged FIR under Section 498A, 406 along with other Sections of IPC against her in-laws.
The matter was amicably settled.

The petitioner, at the time of passing of impugned orders,
was in a vegetative state and he could not participate in the assessment proceedings.
The respondent- department was duly intimated about the health of the petitioner No.1 still ex- parte assessment order was passed.

7. The foundation of impugned assessment orders is FIR No.3 dated 01.01.2001 which stands q u a s h e d b y t h i s C o u r t o n t h e b a s i s o f c o m p r o m i s e 3 o f 4 N e u t r a l C i t a t i o n No:=2024:
- DB CWP-10469-2005 (O&M) -4- arrived at between the parties

. The respondent-department concededly has neither conducted independent investigation nor brought on record evidence to the effect that petitioner actually earned aforesaid amount during the relevant assessment year.

In the absence of any concrete evidence, demand cannot be created on Mohinder Singh & Anr vs Income Tax Officer & Ors on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119969237/
2 assumptions and presumptions.

sentences.text: 8. In the wake of the above facts and findings, we are of the considered opinion that present petition deserves to be allowed and accordingly allowed.

Impugned order dated 30.03.2005 (Annexure P-9)
and all subsequent demand notices are hereby set aside.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

(SHEEL NAGU) (JAGMOHAN BANSAL)
 CHIEF JUSTICE JUDGE 11.07.2024 Mohit Kumar
